en.title: Variables and types
en.intro:
A useful program gives values names that explain their roles. This module starts with one stored message, then asks which kind of value a name holds and what happens when that value is replaced. You will trace the current value at a specific point instead of guessing from a name's spelling. A later lesson distinguishes fixed intent from a language-enforced restriction, and the final lesson converts digit text into a number.

Keep the same code track or compare another language when its note helps. Java's declarations, Python's assignments and JavaScript or TypeScript bindings use different spelling while teaching shared ideas. Fixed values are one important exception: Python's uppercase convention does not enforce the same reassignment restriction as final or const. The course explains that difference rather than pretending every track has identical rules.

Use predictions to make your thinking visible, then run and inspect one small change. The ladder offers a worked binding, completions, a type repair, a register arrangement and an independent digit-slip program. Finish with the checkpoint after closing the examples. You can revisit a rung without losing work in another track; explanations and recall schedules remain local to this device.
en.recallPrompt: Without looking back, how does an unquoted identifier differ from quoted text that happens to spell the same word?
